import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.38

by O. V. Mel'nikov

A variety of profinite groups is a nonempty class closed under closed subgroups,
quotients by closed normal subgroups, and arbitrary Tikhonov products. A subvariety
of the variety $\mathfrak N$ of all pronilpotent groups is called locally nilpotent
if all of its topologically finitely generated groups are nilpotent.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 7.38.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.38»

open CategoryTheory

universe u

/-- A variety of profinite groups is a nonempty class closed under closed subgroups,
quotients by closed normal subgroups, and arbitrary Tikhonov products. Closure under
subgroups and quotients is expressed invariantly using injective and surjective
continuous homomorphisms. -/
def IsProfiniteVariety (V : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  V.Nonempty ∧
    (∀ ⦃G⦄, G ∈ V → ∀ ⦃H⦄ (f : H ⟶ G), Function.Injective f → H ∈ V) ∧
    (∀ ⦃G⦄, G ∈ V → ∀ ⦃H⦄ (f : G ⟶ H), Function.Surjective f → H ∈ V) ∧
    ∀ (ι : Type u) (G : ι → ProfiniteGrp.{u}), (∀ i, G i ∈ V) → ProfiniteGrp.pi G ∈ V

/-- A profinite group is pronilpotent if each of its finite continuous quotients is
nilpotent. -/
def IsPronilpotent (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ (Q : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) (f : G ⟶ Q), Function.Surjective f →
    Finite Q → Group.IsNilpotent Q

/-- A profinite group is pro-$p$ if each of its finite continuous quotients is a
$p$-group. -/
def IsProP (p : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ (Q : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) (f : G ⟶ Q), Function.Surjective f → Finite Q → IsPGroup p Q

/-- A profinite group is topologically finitely generated if some finite set generates
a dense abstract subgroup. -/
def IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set G, S.Finite ∧ (Subgroup.closure S).topologicalClosure = ⊤

/--
Is it true that every non-nilpotent subvariety of the variety $\mathfrak N$ of all
pronilpotent groups contains a non-nilpotent locally nilpotent subvariety?

Here varieties are classes of profinite groups closed under closed subgroups, quotients
by closed normal subgroups, and arbitrary Tikhonov products. “Locally nilpotent” means
that every topologically finitely generated member is nilpotent, while
“non-nilpotent” means that the variety has a member whose underlying abstract group
is not nilpotent.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ V : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}, IsProfiniteVariety V →
      (∀ G ∈ V, IsPronilpotent G) →
      (∃ G ∈ V, ¬ Group.IsNilpotent G) →
      ∃ W : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}, IsProfiniteVariety W ∧ W ⊆ V ∧
        (∃ G ∈ W, ¬ Group.IsNilpotent G) ∧
        ∀ G ∈ W, IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated G → Group.IsNilpotent G := by
  sorry

/--
For each prime $p$, is it true that every non-nilpotent subvariety of the variety of
all pro-$p$ groups contains a non-nilpotent locally nilpotent subvariety?

As in part (a), subvarieties are varieties of profinite groups, “locally nilpotent”
refers to all topologically finitely generated members, and nilpotence is nilpotence
of the underlying abstract group.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∀ V : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}, IsProfiniteVariety V →
      (∀ G ∈ V, IsProP p G) →
      (∃ G ∈ V, ¬ Group.IsNilpotent G) →
      ∃ W : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}, IsProfiniteVariety W ∧ W ⊆ V ∧
        (∃ G ∈ W, ¬ Group.IsNilpotent G) ∧
        ∀ G ∈ W, IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated G → Group.IsNilpotent G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.38»
modeling_decisions: A class of profinite groups is represented at a fixed Lean universe as a set of Mathlib's bundled `ProfiniteGrp` objects.

Closure under closed subgroups is expressed invariantly as closure under domains of injective continuous homomorphisms into a member. For profinite groups, compactness and Hausdorffness make such a map a topological isomorphism onto a closed subgroup.

Closure under factor groups is expressed invariantly as closure under codomains of surjective continuous homomorphisms out of a member. Such a map realizes its target as the quotient by its closed normal kernel.
Arbitrary Tikhonov products are represented by `ProfiniteGrp.pi`; the index type is allowed to be empty, which also enforces membership of the trivial group.
Pronilpotence is modeled by the standard profinite characterization that every finite continuous quotient is nilpotent.
The pro-p condition is modeled by the standard profinite characterization that every finite continuous quotient is a p-group.
Topological finite generation means that the topological closure of the abstract subgroup generated by a finite set is the whole group.
Part (b)'s phrase 'for a given prime p' is represented by universal quantification over natural primes, as required by the decomposition table.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.38

by O. V. Mel'nikov

A *variety of profinite groups* is a non-empty class of profinite groups closed under taking
subgroups, factor-groups, and Tikhonov products. A subvariety $\mathfrak{V}$ of the variety
$\mathfrak{N}$ of all pronilpotent groups is said to be *(locally) nilpotent* if all (finitely
generated) groups in $\mathfrak{V}$ are nilpotent.

a) Is it true that any non-nilpotent subvariety of $\mathfrak{N}$ contains a non-nilpotent
locally nilpotent subvariety?

b) The same problem for the variety of all pro-$p$-groups (for a given prime $p$).

As usual in the theory of profinite groups, "subgroup" means closed subgroup, "factor-group"
means quotient by a closed normal subgroup (equivalently, continuous epimorphic image), and
"finitely generated" means topologically finitely generated, i.e. generated by a finite set as
a topological group. "Nilpotent" is nilpotency of the underlying abstract group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open CategoryTheory

namespace Kourovka.«7.38»

universe u

/-- A profinite group `G` is *pronilpotent* if all of its finite continuous quotients are
nilpotent, i.e. `G ⧸ N` is nilpotent for every open normal subgroup `N` of `G`. Equivalently,
`G` is an inverse limit of finite nilpotent groups. -/
def IsPronilpotent (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ N : OpenNormalSubgroup G, Group.IsNilpotent (G ⧸ N.toSubgroup)

/-- A profinite group `G` is a *pro-`p` group* if all of its finite continuous quotients are
`p`-groups, i.e. `G ⧸ N` is a `p`-group for every open normal subgroup `N` of `G`. Equivalently,
`G` is an inverse limit of finite `p`-groups. -/
def IsProP (p : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ N : OpenNormalSubgroup G, IsPGroup p (G ⧸ N.toSubgroup)

/-- A profinite group `G` is *(topologically) finitely generated* if some finite subset of `G`
generates a dense subgroup of `G`. -/
def IsTopologicallyFG (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Finset G, (Subgroup.closure (S : Set G)).topologicalClosure = ⊤

/-- A *variety of profinite groups* is a non-empty class `𝔙` of profinite groups which is closed
under taking closed subgroups, factor-groups, and Tikhonov products.

Here factor-groups are formalised as continuous epimorphic images: for profinite groups these are
exactly the quotients by closed normal subgroups, and this makes `𝔙` closed under isomorphism.
Tikhonov products are arbitrary direct products, indexed by a type `ι : Type u`, with the product
topology. -/
structure IsVariety (𝔙 : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop where
  nonempty : 𝔙.Nonempty
  ofClosedSubgroup_mem : ∀ G ∈ 𝔙, ∀ H : ClosedSubgroup G, ProfiniteGrp.ofClosedSubgroup H ∈ 𝔙
  mem_of_surjective : ∀ G ∈ 𝔙, ∀ (H : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) (f : G ⟶ H), Function.Surjective f → H ∈ 𝔙
  pi_mem : ∀ {ι : Type u} (G : ι → ProfiniteGrp.{u}), (∀ i, G i ∈ 𝔙) → ProfiniteGrp.pi G ∈ 𝔙

/-- A class `𝔙` of profinite groups is *nilpotent* if all groups in `𝔙` are nilpotent. -/
def IsNilpotentClass (𝔙 : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ G ∈ 𝔙, Group.IsNilpotent G

/-- A class `𝔙` of profinite groups is *locally nilpotent* if all (topologically) finitely
generated groups in `𝔙` are nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotentClass (𝔙 : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ G ∈ 𝔙, IsTopologicallyFG G → Group.IsNilpotent G

/-- Every pro-`p` group is pronilpotent, so part b) is a special case of part a). -/
@[category API, AMS 20 22]
theorem IsProP.isPronilpotent {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}} (h : IsProP p G) :
    IsPronilpotent G :=
  fun N => (h N).isNilpotent

/-- The class of all profinite groups is a variety. -/
@[category test, AMS 20 22]
theorem isVariety_univ : IsVariety (Set.univ : Set ProfiniteGrp.{u}) where
  nonempty := ⟨ProfiniteGrp.of PUnit, Set.mem_univ _⟩
  ofClosedSubgroup_mem _ _ _ := Set.mem_univ _
  mem_of_surjective _ _ _ _ _ := Set.mem_univ _
  pi_mem _ _ := Set.mem_univ _

/--
Is it true that any non-nilpotent subvariety of $\mathfrak{N}$ contains a non-nilpotent locally
nilpotent subvariety?

That is: for every variety $\mathfrak{V}$ of profinite groups all of whose members are
pronilpotent and which contains a non-nilpotent group, is there a variety
$\mathfrak{W} \subseteq \mathfrak{V}$ which contains a non-nilpotent group, but in which
every (topologically) finitely generated group is nilpotent?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka.«7.38».parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ 𝔙 : Set ProfiniteGrp.{0}, IsVariety 𝔙 → (∀ G ∈ 𝔙, IsPronilpotent G) →
      ¬ IsNilpotentClass 𝔙 →
      ∃ 𝔚 : Set ProfiniteGrp.{0}, IsVariety 𝔚 ∧ 𝔚 ⊆ 𝔙 ∧
        ¬ IsNilpotentClass 𝔚 ∧ IsLocallyNilpotentClass 𝔚 := by
  sorry

/--
The same problem for the variety of all pro-$p$-groups (for a given prime $p$): is it true that,
for every prime $p$, any non-nilpotent subvariety of the variety of all pro-$p$-groups contains a
non-nilpotent locally nilpotent subvariety?

That is: for every prime $p$ and every variety $\mathfrak{V}$ of profinite groups all of whose
members are pro-$p$ groups and which contains a non-nilpotent group, is there a variety
$\mathfrak{W} \subseteq \mathfrak{V}$ which contains a non-nilpotent group, but in which
every (topologically) finitely generated group is nilpotent?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 22]
theorem kourovka.«7.38».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime →
      ∀ 𝔙 : Set ProfiniteGrp.{0}, IsVariety 𝔙 → (∀ G ∈ 𝔙, IsProP p G) →
        ¬ IsNilpotentClass 𝔙 →
        ∃ 𝔚 : Set ProfiniteGrp.{0}, IsVariety 𝔚 ∧ 𝔚 ⊆ 𝔙 ∧
          ¬ IsNilpotentClass 𝔚 ∧ IsLocallyNilpotentClass 𝔚 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.38»

'Closed under factor-groups' is formalised as closure under continuous surjective homomorphic images (`f : G ⟶ H` in `ProfiniteGrp`, `Function.Surjective f`). Tikhonov products are formalised via `ProfiniteGrp.pi`, i.e. the direct product with the product topology, over arbitrary index types.

'Finitely generated' is topological finite generation: some finite subset generates a dense subgroup (`(Subgroup.closure S).topologicalClosure = ⊤`). Abstract finite generation would make the question trivial (abstractly f.g. profinite groups are finite).

The notebook defines '(locally) nilpotent' only for subvarieties of 𝔑; the file defines `IsNilpotentClass`/`IsLocallyNilpotentClass` for arbitrary classes, which agrees with the notebook on the varieties to which they are applied.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.38

by O. V. Mel'nikov

A variety of profinite groups is a nonempty class closed under closed subgroups,
factor groups by closed normal subgroups, and arbitrary Tikhonov products. A
subvariety of the variety $\mathfrak N$ of all pronilpotent groups is called
nilpotent if all its groups are nilpotent, and locally nilpotent if all its
topologically finitely generated groups are nilpotent.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.38»

open CategoryTheory

universe u

/-- A profinite group is pronilpotent if each of its finite continuous quotients
is nilpotent. These quotients are represented by open normal subgroups. -/
def IsPronilpotent (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ N : OpenNormalSubgroup G, Group.IsNilpotent (G ⧸ N.toSubgroup)

/-- A profinite group is a pro-$p$ group if each of its finite continuous
quotients is a $p$-group. These quotients are represented by open normal
subgroups. -/
def IsProP (p : ℕ) (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ N : OpenNormalSubgroup G, IsPGroup p (G ⧸ N.toSubgroup)

/-- A profinite group is topologically finitely generated if the topological
closure of the abstract subgroup generated by some finite set is the whole
group. -/
def IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated (G : ProfiniteGrp.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set G, S.Finite ∧ (Subgroup.closure S).topologicalClosure = ⊤

/-- A variety of profinite groups is a nonempty class closed under closed
subgroups, factor groups by closed normal subgroups, and arbitrary Tikhonov
products. Injective and surjective continuous homomorphisms express the first
two closure properties invariantly. -/
def IsVariety (V : ProfiniteGrp.{u} → Prop) : Prop :=
  (∃ G, V G) ∧
  (∀ G H, V G → ∀ f : H ⟶ G, Function.Injective f → V H) ∧
  (∀ G H, V G → ∀ f : G ⟶ H, Function.Surjective f → V H) ∧
  (∀ (ι : Type u) (G : ι → ProfiniteGrp.{u}),
    (∀ i, V (G i)) → V (ProfiniteGrp.pi G))

/-- The variety `W` is a subvariety of `V` if it is itself a variety and every
member of `W` belongs to `V`. -/
def IsSubvariety (W V : ProfiniteGrp.{u} → Prop) : Prop :=
  IsVariety W ∧ ∀ G, W G → V G

/-- A class of profinite groups is non-nilpotent if it contains a group which
is not nilpotent (with nilpotency understood for the underlying abstract
group). -/
def IsNonNilpotent (V : ProfiniteGrp.{u} → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ G, V G ∧ ¬ Group.IsNilpotent G

/-- A class of profinite groups is locally nilpotent if every topologically
finitely generated member is nilpotent as an abstract group. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (V : ProfiniteGrp.{u} → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ G, V G → IsTopologicallyFinitelyGenerated G → Group.IsNilpotent G

/--
Is it true that every non-nilpotent subvariety of the variety
$\mathfrak N$ of all pronilpotent groups contains a non-nilpotent locally
nilpotent subvariety? Here varieties are nonempty classes of profinite groups
closed under closed subgroups, factor groups, and arbitrary Tikhonov products;
"non-nilpotent" means containing a non-nilpotent group, and "locally
nilpotent" means that every topologically finitely generated member is
nilpotent.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem parts.a : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ V : ProfiniteGrp.{u} → Prop,
      IsVariety V →
      (∀ G, V G → IsPronilpotent G) →
      IsNonNilpotent V →
      ∃ W : ProfiniteGrp.{u} → Prop,
        IsSubvariety W V ∧ IsNonNilpotent W ∧ IsLocallyNilpotent W := by
  sorry

/--
For every prime $p$, is it true that every non-nilpotent subvariety of the
variety of all pro-$p$ groups contains a non-nilpotent locally nilpotent
subvariety? Subvarieties and (local) nilpotency have the same meanings as in
part (a), with finite continuous quotients now required to be $p$-groups.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime →
      ∀ V : ProfiniteGrp.{u} → Prop,
        IsVariety V →
        (∀ G, V G → IsProP p G) →
        IsNonNilpotent V →
        ∃ W : ProfiniteGrp.{u} → Prop,
          IsSubvariety W V ∧ IsNonNilpotent W ∧ IsLocallyNilpotent W := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.38»

Characterized pronilpotent and pro-p profinite groups by requiring every quotient by an open normal subgroup to be respectively nilpotent or a p-group; these are exactly the finite continuous quotients of a profinite group.

Encoded closure under closed subgroups invariantly as closure under domains of injective continuous homomorphisms between profinite groups. Such a map from a compact space to a Hausdorff space identifies its domain with a closed subgroup.

Read 'finitely generated' as topologically finitely generated: a finite set generates a subgroup whose topological closure is the whole group.
Used Mathlib's `Group.IsNilpotent`, so nilpotency is that of the underlying abstract group.
Read 'for a given prime p' in part (b) as universal quantification over primes, as required by the decomposition table.
